Command: Rest on the eighth day of Tabernacles
Summary: The eighth day after Tabernacles is kept as a holy convocation of rest, a solemn assembly of its own.
Commandment: Keep the eighth day as a holy convocation and rest on it.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The closing rest gathered the whole feast season to its end in worship. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
Function: The eighth day after Tabernacles was kept as a holy convocation of rest, a solemn assembly of its own — a ceremonial law closing the season. Its goal was to gather the whole feast season to its end in worship, one more day set apart after the seven days of booths. It did not address a particular evil; its work was completion and reverence, not restraint. The eighth day said the season did not just run out; it was closed deliberately, in rest before God.
